tasks.short: Patrol and exercise lawful enforcement judgement

steps.what: Drive vehicles or patrol specific areas to detect law violators
Assess lawful grounds, issue citations, and make arrests where authorised
outputs: lawful enforcement action or no action

tasks.design: Retain physical patrol and each lawful enforcement decision with the officer. Existing policy references in {DOCS} may support work, but this design introduces no automated suspicion, targeting or arrest recommendation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Enforcement depends on facts, lawful grounds and circumstances that can change quickly.
tasks.enabler_now: Reporting and lookup capabilities do not replace field assessment or physical patrol.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing proportionality and uncertainty while protecting people and legal rights.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can reconsider an impression, de-escalate and decide that no action is warranted.
tasks.altitude: No change to patrol time, statutory powers or accountability.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of police and detectives
reach.task: Review a difficult enforcement judgement through existing oversight

evidence.claim: Physical patrol and lawful enforcement remain contextual human work; no incremental software saving is assumed.

assumptions: Boundary is patrol and enforcement, not subsequent case-report drafting. The occupational wording grants no powers beyond local law.
Officer produces scene observations in s1 and assesses them in s2; no structured offence, suspect or threat flag is assumed.
Check native policy-reference access before custom code; existing system runtime earns no saving.
No new tool, monitoring or maintained dataset is introduced, so incremental upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local legal authority and patrol arrangements
research_questions: Where do officers need clearer policy access while retaining independent assessment of facts?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Routine patrol and complex enforcement retain time; separate reporting benefits are excluded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor, investigate, note and report unusual activity and hazards

steps.what: Monitor suspicious situations, safety hazards and unusual activity in patrol area
Investigate observed concerns and distinguish facts from interpretations
Note observed facts, investigation findings and uncertainties
Prepare, check and report relevant findings to appropriate personnel

tasks.design: Configure a source-linked report view inside the authorised police records {OTHER}, reusing facts already entered by the officer. Keep monitoring, investigation, note capture and final meaning checks; the view never labels a person suspicious or generates evidence.
tasks.previous_blocker: An officer may repeat already captured facts in a separate internal report format.
tasks.enabler_now: Native field reuse can reduce duplicate report assembly without summarising or altering free text.
tasks.still_hard: Separating observation from inference and explaining what remains uncertain.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can recognise that an apparent inconsistency needs more investigation rather than a fluent explanation.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeated report entry; investigative judgement stays unchanged.

reach.task: Trace a report statement to the officer's original entry
reach.learn: Source provenance, corrections and access boundaries

evidence.claim: Axon Draft One drafts patrol reports from bodycam audio with officer confirmation; the cited randomised trial did not find faster report writing, so model drafting savings are not assumed.
Native reuse of existing fields can reduce duplicate internal report assembly without a language model; the allocation is an E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is observation, investigation and its initial report, not later full case-file drafting. Overlapping entries must be assigned once in a roll-up.

Officer in s3 captures event ID, date/time, location, source, directly observed facts, attributed statements, investigation findings, uncertainty, actions and intended authorised recipient. Full 20 hours retain all field and narrative capture.
S4 copies exact fields without semantic rewriting; absent details stay explicit. Retained 9 hours include manual exceptions, meaning and source checks and recipient access checks before release.
Test native police-record configuration before custom code; existing automatic report filling earns no new savings.
No public model receives police data and no recording or predictive classification is introduced; access and national consultation requirements are checked during rollout.
unknowns: Native record reuse capabilities and permitted recipients
research_questions: Does exact field reuse remove repetition while preserving attribution, uncertainty and later corrections?

already_counted.description: Report meaning, exceptions and release check

incremental.description: Maintain report fields, access and correction mapping

approvals.approved_version: Exact report snapshot with event, facts, attribution, uncertainty, actions and recipient; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 scenario: B=100 and R=35+30+20+9=94 give gross 6, less 1 upkeep yields net 5. High requires repeated assembly in the 15-hour reporting step; low assumes only 1 hour removed, consumed by upkeep. Monitoring, investigation and note capture retain all time; no model drafting saving is credited.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Investigate accidents and assess causes and possible offences

steps.what: Investigate traffic accidents and other accidents and gather evidence
Determine causes and assess whether a crime has been committed

tasks.design: Keep accident investigation and reasoned findings with the officer using authorised evidence in {DOCS}. This design introduces no automated causal verdict, offence classification or evidence-reliability score.
tasks.previous_blocker: An accident can have competing explanations and incomplete or conflicting evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Search and document tools can support access but do not establish the cause or legal conclusion.
tasks.still_hard: Testing alternative explanations and distinguishing a possible offence from insufficient evidence.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can seek missing evidence, question assumptions and explain uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Investigation time and statutory decision boundaries remain unchanged.

reach.task: Review a complex accident evidence gap
reach.learn: Evidence preservation and limits of causal inference

evidence.claim: Accident cause and possible offence assessment require contextual evidence evaluation; existing document access alone earns no new saving.

assumptions: Boundary is investigation and findings, not separate report formatting or a court's determination of guilt.
Officer gathers evidence in s1 before assessing it in s2; no structured cause or criminality label is assumed.
Native evidence-reference facilities should be assessed before custom code.
No new tool, dataset or monitoring is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local investigation scope and specialist referral arrangements
research_questions: Which evidence gaps require specialist reconstruction rather than more document searching?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Straightforward and contested accidents retain evidence gathering and reasoning time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Relay complaints and emergency requests to dispatchers

steps.what: Relay complaint and emergency-request information to appropriate agency dispatchers

tasks.design: Retain officer relay and confirmation through operational radio or telephone {OTHER}. No automatic dispatch priority or agency allocation is introduced, and missing location or request details are clarified through the existing channel.
tasks.previous_blocker: Urgent accounts may be incomplete and require clarification and acknowledgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing communication technology supports relay but does not remove the need to establish shared understanding.
tasks.still_hard: Communicating uncertainty and recognising an incorrect or incomplete understanding promptly.
tasks.human_edge: The officer can ask a targeted question and recognise when a request needs immediate clarification.
tasks.altitude: Relay time and dispatcher authority remain unchanged.

reach.role: first-line supervisor of police and detectives
reach.task: Resolve an uncertain escalation route through existing procedures

evidence.claim: Emergency relay requires clarification and acknowledgement; no saving is established by existing channel runtime.

assumptions: Boundary is officer relay; dispatcher assessment and allocation labour remain outside the focal role and are not claimed saved.
Officer captures and clarifies information during s1; no structured address, urgency code or automatic routing contract is assumed.
Review native communication capabilities before future custom code.
No new tool, recording or maintained routing dataset is introduced, so upkeep is zero.
unknowns: Local relay and inter-agency communication procedures
research_questions: What missing details most often require a relay clarification, and how is acknowledgement confirmed?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and upkeep=0 give zero saving. Routine complaints and urgent requests retain clarification and relay time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep patrol, enforcement, investigation and emergency communication human; reduce only demonstrated duplicate internal report assembly.
reach: Help records colleagues trace exact facts and corrections to original officer entries
role.ambitious_version: An officer who can explain the evidence and uncertainty behind actions without repeated reporting or expanded automated enforcement.
